pr_title: locale-util: extend comments on unicode glyph use, and drop mdash (th…
pr_body:
…at actually was an ndash)

Let's add the actual unicode names of the glyphs we use. Let's also add
in comments what the width expectations of these glyphs are on the
console.

Also, remove the "mdash" definition. First of all it wasn't used, but
what's worse the glyph encoded was actually an "ndash"...

Fixes: #14075

issue_context.title: src/basic/locale-util.c variable vs glyph inconsistency
issue_context.body:
$ grep CROSS ./src/basic/locale-util.c | tail -n 1
                        [SPECIAL_GLYPH_CROSS_MARK]              = "\342\234\227",             /* ✗ */

The variable name refers to U+274C CROSS MARK but the code point (as well as the glyph in the comment) is actually U+2717 BALLOT X. This inconsistency should be fixed either by renaming the variable or correcting the codepoint (and the comment).
comments:
Those names are not unicode names. E.g. SPECIAL_GLYPH_ECSTATIC_SMILEY
is called 'SMILING FACE WITH HALO' and so on. We want the "ballot x"
character, because unicode 'CROSS MARK' is big and red and does not fit,
but SPECIAL_GLYPH_CROSS_MARK is a more descriptive name.

I think there's nothing to fix here.

Zbyszek
(I think it wouldn't hurt adding comments referencing the unicode names though)

review_comments:
I think `m-x describe-char` or the equivalent in other editors would be a good enough solution, without the risk of the comments getting out of date. But since you already did the work, OK ;)

LGTM.
